title: HRA for Non-Salaried: Understanding Section 80GG
description: Non-salaried individuals, including self-employed, cannot claim House Rent Allowance (HRA) but can claim a similar deduction under Section 80GG of the Income .

faq.q: Who is eligible to claim a deduction under Section 80GG?
faq.a: Individuals and HUFs who do not receive HRA from an employer and pay rent for their accommodation are eligible. They must not own a residential property in the city of their residence and employment.

faq.q: Is Form 10BA mandatory for claiming 80GG deduction?
faq.a: Yes, filing Form 10BA is mandatory to claim the deduction under Section 80GG. It is a declaration that you meet all the prescribed conditions.

faq.q: What is "Adjusted Gross Total Income" for 80GG calculation?
faq.a: It's your Gross Total Income minus all Chapter VI-A deductions (like 80C, 80D, etc.) except 80GG itself, and excluding certain capital gains and other specified incomes.

faq.q: Can I claim 80GG if I own a house in another city?
faq.a: Yes, you can claim 80GG if you own a house in another city, provided you do not reside in that house and do not claim it as self-occupied under Section 23(2)(a) or 23(2)(b) of the Income Tax Act.

faq.q: What is the maximum deduction allowed under Section 80GG?
faq.a: The maximum deduction allowed under Section 80GG is capped at ₹60,000 per financial year (₹5,000 per month).

faq.q: Do I need to provide rent receipts for 80GG?
faq.a: While rent receipts are not directly uploaded with Form 10BA, it is crucial to keep them as proof. The Income Tax Department may ask for them during assessment.
